title: The Pale Winter Anew
premise: Casper Ashgrove hosts a late-night call-in show in the snowbound town of Hollowmere, where the callers all turn out to be townsfolk who died within the past week — and every one of them hums the same half-finished folk song. When an excavation crew on the old Ashgrove land unearths an iron door sealed from the inside, the diggers vanish into it one by one, and Casper discovers his family inherited not the estate but the duty of keeping the door's occupant asleep. The dead teach him the song's final verse, but singing it means joining them; the only other way to close the door forever is for someone who loves him to sing it in his place. Casper's estranged wife, Wren, returns to Hollowmere, and in the end she sings the last verse alone while Casper, refusing to let her pay his family's price, breaks the inheritance instead — burning the Ashgrove ledger and going silent on air, leaving the door shut, the dead finally quiet, and himself half-heard ever after.
about_author: Ines Coldharbour is the pen name of a former night-shift radio producer who spent a decade answering calls from strangers at 3 a.m. and never quite stopped wondering who was on the other end. She writes in an unheated farmhouse and claims the cold keeps the sentences honest.

chapters.title: Dead Air
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. A routine broadcast until a caller describes her own funeral from last Tuesday. Casper assumes a prank; the emotional beat is professional detachment curdling into unease as the woman hums a tune he half-recognizes from childhood.

chapters.title: The Hollowmere Frequency
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. He checks the caller's name against the obituaries and finds it exact. Denial hardens into obsession; he replays the tape all night, hearing beneath the static the same melody in every call.

chapters.title: Excavation at Ashgrove Field
chapters.summary: Foreman Dara Okonjo's POV. The crew breaks frost on the old Ashgrove parcel and strikes iron instead of stone — a door, its hinges rusted shut, its bolts thrown from within. Dara feels watched; the beat is workmanlike confidence beginning to fray.

chapters.title: Calls from the Recently Departed
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Three dead callers in one night, each humming the song a little further along. He visits the grave of the first caller and finds fresh flowers he didn't leave; dread replaces disbelief.

chapters.title: Wren
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, arriving in Hollowmere after two years apart, summoned by a voicemail Casper doesn't remember leaving. The beat is wary tenderness — old love meeting old wounds in a town gone strangely quiet.

chapters.title: Sealed from the Inside
chapters.summary: Dara's POV. Locksmiths refuse the door; a camera lowered to the seam shows warmth blooming like breath on glass. One digger, Pell, starts humming at the site and can't stop. Foreboding builds.

chapters.title: The Ashgrove Ledger
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. In his grandmother's attic he finds a ledger of names, dates, and verses — generations of Ashgroves, each entry ending with the same instruction: learn the last, never sing along. The inheritance reveals itself as a debt.

chapters.title: Pell Stops Coming Home
chapters.summary: Dara's POV. Pell vanishes between shifts; his boots are found neatly by the door, facing it. The crew wants to quit; the county wants the road. Guilt and denial war in Dara.

chapters.title: Verse by Verse
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. A dead choir teacher calls and, gently, begins teaching him the song, stopping short of the final verse. The beat is seduction — the dead are patient, kind, and absolutely certain he'll want to finish it.

chapters.title: The Town That Hums
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. She notices shopkeepers pausing mid-sentence to hum; church bells play the melody wrong on purpose. Hollowmere knows the song and is pretending not to. Isolation closes around her.

chapters.title: On-Air Confession
chapters.summary: Casper's POV, live broadcast. He asks listeners if anyone else has heard the dead. The switchboard lights up — the living, this time, all humming. He realizes the whole town is a congregation.

chapters.title: What the Door Wants
chapters.summary: Dara's POV, dream sequence bleeding into waking: the door in her dreams is open, and something on the other side is politely waiting to be sung to. She wakes with dirt under her nails.

chapters.title: The Last Ashgrove
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. She reads the ledger over sleeping Casper's shoulder and understands his family kept the door fed with verses — and with Ashgroves. The beat is horror at what love in this family has always cost.

chapters.title: Dara Descends
chapters.summary: Dara's POV. She returns alone to the door with a crowbar and a recorder. The iron is warm. Her recording captures her own voice answering herself in an older dialect. She runs; the humming follows her truck home.

chapters.title: The Verse That Isn't There
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. He asks the dead callers for the final verse; each goes silent mid-hum, terrified. Even the dead won't sing it. The beat shifts from seduction to threat — the song wants a living voice.

chapters.title: Coldharbour Road
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Following the ledger's oldest entry, she walks to a ruined chapel and meets an ancient caretaker who remembers the first Ashgrove: a man who bargained with the door to save his dying town, and bound his blood to the bargain.

chapters.title: The First Bargain
chapters.summary: The caretaker's tale, framed in Casper's POV as Wren recounts it. The door was sealed from the inside by the thing that sleeps behind it — it locked itself in, and the song is the lullaby that keeps it there. The price: a verse-keeper in every generation.

chapters.title: Dara's Last Broadcast
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Dara calls the show, humming, her speech dissolving into the melody. He traces the call to the excavation site and drives out through the snow. Guilt and urgency peak; he arrives to find her boots by the door.

chapters.title: Boots Facing the Door
chapters.summary: Casper's POV at the site. He touches the iron and it breathes. The door knows his name, his blood, his voice — it has been waiting for the last Ashgrove to come sing it to sleep. He flees, but part of him wanted to stay.

chapters.title: Wren's Condition
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. She confronts Casper; he confesses everything, including the ledger's final page: the last verse can only be sung by someone the door-keeper loves, given freely. She realizes why she was summoned — or why she came. The beat is heartbreak.

chapters.title: The Town Remembers
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs braided. Hollowmere stops pretending: shops close, the church fills, the whole town hums in unison at dusk. The congregation isn't worshipping the thing — they're feeding it, keeping it drowsy, and they need the last verse soon.

chapters.title: Half the Song
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. He practices the verses he has, refusing the last, and notices each rehearsal makes the radio crackle with voices a little closer. Learning the song is opening the door a crack. The beat is the trap closing.

chapters.title: The Caretaker's Warning
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The caretaker dies mid-sentence, humming, and his chapel goes dark. His last words: the door doesn't want a lullaby anymore — it wants a duet. Something behind the iron has begun singing back.

chapters.title: Static Choir
chapters.summary: Casper's final broadcast. He plays the dead callers' recordings on air as a warning; instead, every radio in town plays them back in harmony, and the harmony includes a voice that was never human. Panic and exaltation split the town.

chapters.title: The Dig Reopens
chapters.summary: Dara's POV — returned from the dead, or something wearing her. She leads the county crew back to the door with orders to open it. Casper and Wren watch from the ridge, unable to stop it, as the first bolt slides free from inside.

chapters.title: What Casper Won't Do
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. He decides to sing the last verse himself, love or no love, and let the door take an Ashgrove as it always has. Wren catches him rehearsing it in the dark and hears the whole verse at last — the beat is furious, terrified love.

chapters.title: The Ledger Burns
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. She burns the ledger to sever the inheritance, and every dead caller goes silent mid-hum. The silence is worse: the thing behind the door is now awake enough to sing its own half, and the song is decaying without a keeper.

chapters.title: Frostline
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Winter deepens unnaturally; the frost creeps inward from the field in a perfect circle around the buried door. The town evacuates or stays to hum. Casper and Wren, now allies in guilt, plan something neither will say aloud: each intends to sing alone.

chapters.title: The Door Unbolted
chapters.summary: Dara's POV, fragmenting. The last bolt draws back; the door opens inward onto warmth and a vast, patient dark that is not empty. Dara steps through willingly, smiling, and the door begins to close behind her — but not all the way.

chapters.title: A Crack of Warmth
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. Through the door's remaining gap he hears the thing's verse — the answering half of the song, beautiful and wrong. He understands: the last verse isn't a lullaby anymore. It's an invitation, and the door has been waiting for someone to accept.

chapters.title: Two Voices
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. She and Casper admit their plans to each other and fight — the book's emotional nadir, love against duty made literal. They agree on a lie: they'll go together. Each privately means to push the other back and sing alone.

chapters.title: The Congregation Gathers
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The town that remains assembles at the field at midnight, humming the half-song as the frost circle tightens. The dead stand among them, visible now, mouths moving. The beat is terrible communal beauty.

chapters.title: Casper at the Threshold
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. He stands before the open door, the last verse in his throat, and hears his grandmother's voice among the dead — not urging him on, but begging him to stop. He realizes the inheritance was never duty. It was a cage the Ashgroves built around their own guilt.

chapters.title: Wren's Verse
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. She steps past him and begins the last verse, freely given, her voice steady. The door swings wide; the dark leans in to harmonize. Casper, instead of pulling her back, does the thing no Ashgrove ever did — he joins her.

chapters.title: The Broken Inheritance
chapters.summary: Climax, Casper's POV. Two living voices sing the final verse together — not as keeper and sacrifice, but as a duet the bargain never anticipated. The song, completed in love rather than duty, turns inside out. The door slams; the bolts throw themselves from the inside, sealing the thing in with its own unfinished half.

chapters.title: Silence on the Frequency
chapters.summary: Casper's POV, aftermath. The dead are gone — truly gone, their calls unanswered, their graves just graves. The station's transmitter burns out mid-broadcast. Casper signs off with words no one hears, and the beat is grief and release braided together.

chapters.title: What the Town Kept
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Hollowmere thaws; the hum fades from the streets, though some older residents still pause at dusk, listening for a melody that no longer comes. Dara's boots remain by the door, now welded shut under concrete and snow.

chapters.title: The Half-Heard Man
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. He takes a new job reading news at dawn, voice damaged from the singing — half-heard, always slightly staticky. Wren stays. The beat is quiet repair: love that survived the door, priced but not paid in blood.

chapters.title: Letters to the Dead
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Listeners write to the defunct show addressed to their dead; Casper reads them aloud to an empty studio each night, not as a séance but as a memorial. The inheritance is broken, but the remembering is chosen now, not owed.

chapters.title: The Pale Winter Anew
chapters.summary: Final chapter, both POVs braided. A year later, first snow falls on the sealed field. Casper's radio, unplugged, crackles once with a hum — a single bar, then nothing, perhaps only the wind. He and Wren hold each other in the doorway of their home, facing out, and do not answer. The beat is earned peace with a hairline fracture of doubt running through it.
